clues: This city is in east China, in a rich delta land. It grew by the Grand Canal, where boats once brought trade and art.
Cold winds blow from far north lands in winter and can push nights below freezing. Warm south winds in summer can push the heat high.
This city was founded in 514 BC, long ago. It grew fast in the Han age as folks moved here from the north.
Its prize gardens blend homes, water, rocks, and plants in one calm scene. Each one looks like a poem of nature made in stone and green.
Its old gardens hold a place on the world heritage list. They were first put on that list in 1997, and more joined in 2000.
